product.name: Engineering protocols
product.lede: Engineering protocols state what makes engineering work legitimate: which claims must hold, which evidence counts and for which revision, which actions need authority, and which outcomes a case can end in.
product.meta: Rust · protocols as Canon protocol/1 data · Apache-2.0

sections.title: Engineering method, declared as data.
sections.lede: This project owns the engineering vocabulary and the protocols written in it. What a claim, a piece of evidence or an obligation is, and how one is decided, belongs to Canon.

items.title: Protocols are data
items.description: Each protocol is a Canon protocol/1 document at protocols/<name>/<major>.yaml. Canon validates it, compiles it and evaluates it; engineering protocols add no hidden clock, network or model call.

items.title: UNKNOWN is not FALSE
items.description: Tests that passed on revision R1 say nothing about R2: tests.pass is UNKNOWN and merge stays blocked until evidence for R2 exists. Missing or stale evidence never makes a claim FALSE.

items.title: Delivery and incidents
items.description: Every rule is pressure-tested against software delivery and incident response. An incident can leave emergency mode while its cause is still UNKNOWN.

sections.title: From a protocol to a page.
sections.lede: A protocol is written once as data. Canon checks and compiles it, and every page on this site is generated from that compiled form.
